neighbours.label: The closing punctuation of a short quoted utterance in narrative (the '!"', ',"' or '."' that ends direct speech), vs the same content reported indirectly; weak unit
fire: The guard raised his hand and barked, "Nobody leaves this room!"
"Keep the change," the old man said, pushing the coins across the counter.
As the boat tipped, Sam yelled, "Hold on to the rope!"
"We're almost there," whispered the guide as the path narrowed.
The coach leaned in and told them, "Just play your game."
"Don't touch that," Mia warned, grabbing her brother's arm.
From the back of the hall someone shouted, "Louder, please!"
"It's only a scratch," he insisted, wrapping his hand in a towel.
quiet: The guard raised his hand and ordered everyone to stay in the room.
The old man told the cashier to keep the change and pushed the coins across.
As the boat tipped, Sam yelled at the others to hold on to the rope.
The guide whispered that they were almost there as the path narrowed.
The coach leaned in and told them to just play their game.
Mia warned her brother not to touch it and grabbed his arm.
From the back of the hall someone asked the speaker to talk louder.
He insisted it was only a scratch and wrapped his hand in a towel.

predictions: Quoted direct speech reaches 0.10-0.2 at the closing quote; indirect speech stays near 0.03. Activations are low overall, so the test may fail on magnitude.
notes: Card: peaks on ',"', '."\n', '!"', closing quotes of short spoken lines ("Let them eat all they want," says...). Probe: '!"' 0.155, '"I'll be back,"' 0.150, '"Look at this,"' 0.108; narrative without quotes 0.023-0.051; the aphorism without line break 0.027.
